Why Choose One Over the Other

Controlled inputs are the default recommendation for most application forms because validation, conditional disabling, formatting-as-you-type, and multi-field dependencies (a "confirm password" field checked against "password") all need the current value available in JavaScript on every keystroke — which is exactly what controlled state provides for free.
Uncontrolled inputs earn their place in narrower situations: a single free-text field read only at submit time with no live validation, a file input (
cannot be set programmatically by React or anything else, for browser security reasons — it is
uncontrolled), or a form embedded inside a performance-sensitive list where re-rendering on every keystroke is measurably too expensive.
